title: Open Models for Civic Good
text:
What we’ll build
An “Ask Your City Council” tool:

An open-weight model running on your laptop
Answers questions about public meeting minutes
In plain language, citing the page behind every fact
Says “I couldn’t find that” instead of guessing

You need basic Python and Git. No GPU, no ML background, no paid account. ~90 minutes for the core build.

title: Open Models for Civic Good
section: Why open models for civic work?
text:
Why open models for civic work?


Public data stays under public control. Nothing leaves your machine.
Free to run. A city, library or nonprofit pays no per-query API bill.
Inspectable. Anyone can read, fork and improve the code, which matters when residents need to trust the answers.

text:
How it works: RAG

Once MinutesPDF · txt · md → OCRif scanned → Page-taggedchunks → Vectorindex


Each question Resident’squestion → Find 5 closestchunks → Model answersONLY from them → Plain answer+ citations

Retrieval-augmented generation: the model answers from the records, not its memory. That’s what makes citations possible.

title: Open Models for Civic Good
text:
Get the documents

Download 3–10 recent minutes or agendas into docs/
Example: City of Oakwood, Ohio council minutes








Oakwood’s minutes are scans from an office copier


pypdf finds 0 characters on every page. Without OCR, the tool answers every question with “I couldn’t find that.”

title: Open Models for Civic Good
text:
OCR: make scanned minutes searchable
brew install ocrmypdf          # macOS
sudo apt install ocrmypdf      # Ubuntu / Debian (Windows: use WSL)


ocr.py

def ocr_folder(src="docs", dst="docs_ocr"):
    out_dir = pathlib.Path(dst)
    out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for pdf in sorted(pathlib.Path(src).glob("*.pdf")):
        out = out_dir / pdf.name
        print(f"OCR: {pdf.name}")
        ocrmypdf.ocr(pdf, out, language="eng", skip_text=True,
                     deskew=True, rotate_pages=True, progress_bar=False)
        check(out)

def check(pdf):
    """Flag pages where OCR found little text, so a person can look at them."""
    for n, page in enumerate(PdfReader(pdf).pages, start=1):
        if len((page.extract_text() or "").strip()) < 200:
            print(f"  check {pdf.name} p. {n}")

0 → 4,603
characters on the densest page
9 pages in about 17 seconds

Check before you trust it:

Roll-call lines with dot leaders turned to junk, and a council member’s name was misread
“Pickleball” became “picklebal]”
Printed page numbers (386–394) ≠ PDF pages (1–9)

Spot-check names, votes and dollar amounts against the scan.



For tougher scans (handwriting, stamps, tables), use an open vision model on just the flagged pages: Gemma 4’s image input at a high token budget, or Ai2’s fully open olmOCR.

section: ask.py: the prompt does the civic work
text:
ask.py: the prompt does the civic work
SYSTEM = """You help residents understand their local government.
Use ONLY the excerpts provided. Do not use outside knowledge.
Write in plain language at about an 8th-grade reading level.
After each fact, cite its excerpt exactly as labeled,
like [minutes.pdf, p. 4] or [notes.md, lines 12-30].
If the excerpts do not answer the question, say:
"I couldn't find that in these records."
Then suggest contacting the city clerk.
Never guess names, dates, dollar amounts, or vote counts."""

title: Open Models for Civic Good
section: ask.py: retrieve, then stream the answer
text:
ask.py: retrieve, then stream the answer
def stream_answer(question):
    hits = retrieve(question)              # 5 closest chunks
    context = "\n\n".join(
        f"Excerpt [{h['source']}, {h['loc']}]:\n{h['text']}"
        for h in hits)
    stream = client.chat(
        model="gemma4:e4b",
        messages=[system_msg, user_msg(context, question)],
        think=False,       # skip Gemma 4's silent "thinking" pass
        stream=True,       # print words as they arrive
        keep_alive="30m",
        options={"temperature": 0.2, "num_predict": 600})
    for part in stream:
        yield part["message"]["content"]

title: Open Models for Civic Good
text:
“ask.py just hangs”
Gemma 4 is a reasoning model. By default it may think silently for minutes on a laptop CPU, with nothing on screen.



Fix
Why




think=False
Skip the hidden reasoning pass


stream=True
Words appear as they’re written


num_predict: 600
Cap runaway answers


Client(timeout=300)
Give up instead of hanging forever


check_setup()
Clear error if Ollama or a model is missing



Still slow? Run ollama ps. “100% CPU” → switch to gemma4:e2b. The first question is always slower while the model loads.

title: Open Models for Civic Good
section: app.py: a page residents can use
text:
app.py: a page residents can use
import gradio as gr
from ask import check_setup, stream_answer

def respond(message, history):
    text = ""
    for piece in stream_answer(message):
        text += piece
        yield text                     # stream into the chat

demo = gr.ChatInterface(
    fn=respond,
    title="Ask Your City Council",
    description="Answers come only from published records, "
                "with citations.",
)
check_setup()
demo.launch()

trends.py: 311 requests vs. budget
Pandas does the math. The model only explains the table.
def demand_vs_budget(csv_311, csv_budget, categories=None):
    counts = requests_by_year(csv_311, categories)
    budget = pd.read_csv(csv_budget)
    out = counts.merge(budget, on=["year", "category"], how="left")
    g = out.sort_values(["category", "year"]).groupby("category")
    out["requests_change_pct"] = g["requests"].pct_change() * 100
    out["budget_change_pct"] = g["budget_usd"].pct_change() * 100
    out["usd_per_request"] = out["budget_usd"] / out["requests"]
    return out

title: Open Models for Civic Good
text:
The question

“What are the trends for potholes, trash and other complaints, and what is the top complaint?”

Data: Dayton’s Calls for Service dataset · 25,824 police calls, Aug 6 – Oct 4, 2026

How AI helped:

Read the file first: police dispatches, not 311, so no pothole category exists
Code did the counting, not the model’s memory
Fair comparisons: resident calls only, two full four-week windows
Plain-language results with the caveats a council member needs

title: Open Models for Civic Good
section: What the data can’t tell you
text:
What the data can’t tell you

Potholes: not here. Residents report them to the city, not police.
Trash: ~5 dumping calls a week is too few for a trend.
Budget renewal: 8 weeks can’t show year-over-year growth.
Big swings need a reason: the tree-down drop may be one August storm.


Dayton’s service-request data: residents report potholes and dumping through Dayton Delivers or daytonohio.gov (937-333-3333). Look on the Dayton Transparency Portal; if it isn’t published, file a public records request for 2+ years.

title: Open Models for Civic Good
text:
Responsible civic AI checklist



Cite or stay silent
Label it as AI, not an official service
Keep personal data local
Public records only
Write plainly (8th-grade level)



Accessible UI (keyboard, contrast, screen readers)
Test for uneven quality across neighborhoods and languages
Human review for translations and alt text
Check licenses: model, data, yours
Document limits in the README



A wrong answer about a tax deadline or a benefit rule can cost someone real money.
